pr_title: use `cty.DynamicVal` for expanded resources during validation
pr_body:
Revert the evaluation change from #29862.

While returning a dynamic value for all expanded resources during validation is not optimal, trying to work around this using unknown maps and lists is causing other undesirable behaviors during evaluation.

Fixes #30127
pr_comments:
I'm going to lock this pull request because it has been closed for _30 days_ ⏳. This helps our maintainers find and focus on the active contributions.
If you have found a problem that seems related to this change, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.

issue_context.title: Terraform 1.1.0 lookup regression
issue_context.body:
After upgrading to terraform 1.1.0 from 1.0.11 following expression stopped working:
```
output "sg_id" {
  value = lookup(aws_security_group.lambda_default_sg, "default", { id = null })["id"]
}
```

### Expected Behavior
Plan runs fine

### Actual Behavior
```
Invalid value for "default" parameter: the default value must have the same type as the map elements.
```
comments:
Hi @vladimirtiukhtin, thanks for reporting this.

To allow us to reproduce the bug, can you share more of your configuration? I assume that you are using `for_each` with the `aws_security_group.lambda_default_sg`. If so, what is the value used as the expression with the `for_each`?

Anything else you can share about your configuration might help. Thanks in advance!

Hi @vladimirtiukhtin,

Can you confirm whether you were able to _apply_ a plan based on this expression in Terraform v1.0? Terraform v1.1 does include some enhancements to detect certain type inconsistencies sooner (during the plan phase rather than during the apply phase) but we had not intended to introduce any _new_ checks, only to make existing checks happen earlier.

This expression is invalid per the implementation of `lookup`, as @alisdair noted, so if you _were_ able to apply a change containing this expression under Terraform v1.0 then I think our next step would be to try to explain why that is, since that would suggest that there was a previously-undetected bug in Terraform v1.0 which we have inadvertently "fixed" now, and we'll need to therefore do some analysis to try to understand the relative impact between preserving that bug for compatibility or fixing the bug, considering this as a "late-reported regression" as described in [the pragmatic exceptions to our Terraform v1.0 Compatibility Promises](https://www.terraform.io/docs/language/v1-compatibility-promises.html#pragmatic-exceptions) after we've understood how many versions that bug had been present.
Hi @apparentlymart. Yes, as I mentioned at the beginning, this expression runs perfectly fine on terraform 1.0.11

Hello,

I have something similar here, with a new type check error in 1.1.0 (No error previously):

```
│ Error: Inconsistent conditional result types
│ 
│   on agent.tf line 144, in locals:
│  144:   _instances = var.spot ? aws_spot_instance_request.agent : aws_instance.agent
│     ├────────────────
│     │ aws_instance.agent is a list of object, known only after apply
│     │ aws_spot_instance_request.agent is a list of object, known only after apply
│     │ var.spot is a bool, known only after apply
│ 
│ The true and false result expressions must have consistent types. The given
│ expressions are list of object and list of object, respectively.
```
Source code here: https://github.com/Accelize/acid/blob/48639cb0006493612c42e083cd30b254e9f32543/agents/awsEc2/agent.tf#L144

Depending the condition, the object can be "aws_instance" or "aws_spot_instance_request".

We are also seeing this...

`acl_id          = lookup(ibm_is_network_acl.multizone_acl, each.key, { id : null }).id`

is giving:
```
╷
│ Error: Invalid function argument
│ 
│   on .terraform/modules/vpc/main.tf line 66, in module "vpc_subnets":
│   66:   acl_id          = lookup(ibm_is_network_acl.multizone_acl, each.key, { id : null }).id
│ 
│ Invalid value for "default" parameter: the default value must have the same
│ type as the map elements.
╵
```

Works fine on version 1.0.11

Hi all,

We're still investigating this to understand why exactly this had been working in v1.0. So far it seems like what was happening was that Terraform was not fully resolving the resource to a final value before evaluating the output value and so the result of these expressions had previously been "unknown" (how Terraform represents "(known after apply)" internally). Since unknown is not a valid value for an output value, Terraform would then save it as `null` in the state snapshot, making it seem as if you'd successfully selected the `null` from the fallback value even though the `null` result was actually for an entirely different reason.

We're considering options for how to move forward from here within the conflicting demands of the compatibility promises, but in case any if you are blocked by this and want to move forward without waiting for a new release containing a fix, there's a different way to write an expression like this which should avoid this quirk, due to [the `try` function](https://www.terraform.io/docs/language/functions/try.html) having a more general design than `lookup` does:

```hcl
  value = try(aws_security_group.lambda_default_sg["default"].id, null)
```

I'm going to lock this issue because it has been closed for _30 days_ ⏳. This helps our maintainers find and focus on the active issues.
If you have found a problem that seems similar to this, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.

review_comments: Given that we were all so surprised that this had ever worked before, I think it would help to include a comment here explaining _why_ the behavior described by this test is "correct", because I expect that in the far future we'll end up back here after seeing this test fail and have lost the context for what exactly this is testing, and thus might end up incorrectly concluding that the test is wrong.
Thanks, I meant to add that and will include it before merging!
